mythos.tagline: The truth is on a commercial break.
mythos.description: A questionable question. Made-up answers. A TV show where nonsense deserves a standing ovation.
mythos.example: Why do socks disappear? “They have formed a union.”
mythos.rules: Write in secret, discover anonymous answers, then vote for your favourite invention. You cannot vote for yourself.

pitch.tagline: The future did not ask for this.
pitch.description: Invent something utterly unsellable. Hand it to another player. Watch them try to make a fortune.
pitch.example: The Depressed Fridge: it cries whenever you open it. Sell it as the next big thing.
pitch.rules: Create an invention or ask House Decoy for an idea. Another player sells it. Rate each presentation for humour, conviction and creativity.

court.description: Defendant, prosecutor, lawyer, judge and jury: a ridiculous crime awaits a far too serious hearing.
court.example: The charge: privately owning the neighbourhood’s last ray of sunshine. Plead your case.
court.rules: Discover your private role, prepare your case, then take the floor. The host directs the hearing. Only the jury decides the verdict.

who.tagline: Your friends already have a suspect.
who.description: You know each other so well… until the show asks exactly the wrong question.
who.example: Who among us would last the shortest time without an undo button?
who.rules: Choose a person on your phone. Discover the group’s verdict together. A no-points mode lets you play just for the laughs.

captions.description: Real film scenes. Your dialogue travels from phone to phone. Then someone has to dare to perform the movie.
captions.example: A dramatic look. A solemn declaration: “I ate the proof of address.”
captions.rules: Write a line for your private frame. Continue another player’s story on the next turn. Finally, dub the movie out loud and award three prizes.
